findingDetails.title: Claude and Pi can select a transcript from a different project when project paths collide
findingDetails.description: Lossy project path keys collide for distinct paths; the default selector picks the newest transcript without verifying project identity, then sweeps it into the current project's queue.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both default selectors are called when no --transcript is supplied, and each sweep appends to the current projectDir queue.

claimAdjudication.claim: The default Claude and Pi transcript selectors can return another project's transcript because their project-directory keys are not injective and they do not validate project identity after selection.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Compared other selectors: Devin and OpenCode query by working directory, while Codex checks transcript cwd. No equivalent identity check appears in Claude or Pi default selectors.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The runtime may retain canonical project identity in transcript metadata, but these selectors do not inspect it before returning the latest file.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if the runtime directory scheme is shown collision-resistant or the selected transcript is validated against canonical current project path before sweep.

findingDetails.title: A closing code or quotation paragraph can be emitted as a chat question
findingDetails.description: The closing paragraph only checks for a question mark, while earlier paragraphs pass through prose() which removes code and quotations.
findingDetails.scopeProof: All transcript sweeps call chatCandidatesFromTurns and its closing branch controls final-paragraph candidate creation.

results.notes: Correctness behavior checked; complete phase acceptance mapping is deferred.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: The target spans multiple runtime transcript selectors, shared capture logic, save wiring, matchers, and phase documentation.

targetSelection.selectionReason: Started at transcript selectors and the shared chat-candidate producer because these feed operator decisions into the queue and save path.

searchLedger.hypothesis: Lossy project-path keys can direct a sweep to another project's transcript.

searchActions.result: Both transforms collide for /work/foo-bar and /work/foo/bar; the latest selector returns a file without checking its project identity, and the sweep queues its records for current projectDir.

searchLedger.rationale: A valid pair of project paths deterministically collides and leads to wrong-project queue writes.

searchLedger.invariant: Question marks in code or quoted text must not qualify a candidate when prose() screens those contexts.

searchActions.result: The final-paragraph branch checks includes('?') without calling asks()/prose(), while non-closing paragraphs use that filter.

searchLedger.rationale: A closing code or quotation paragraph containing '?' is emitted as a candidate.
